candidates.change_summary: Replace call to withdraw(address(this).balance) with direct transfer of entire balance to msg.sender, changing who receives funds when withdrawAll is called (uses transfer instead of internal call).
Change withdrawAll to call withdraw with zero value instead of full balance, causing no funds to be sent on withdrawAll.
Modify onlyOwner modifier to invert the ownership check, allowing only non-owners to call withdrawAll and thus changing whether funds can be withdrawn by the original owner.
Make withdrawAll public with no onlyOwner guard (remove the modifier), allowing anyone to withdraw the contract balance.
Change transfer target from msg.sender to owner so withdraw sends funds to owner instead of the caller.
Relax onlyOwner check to allow anyone to call guarded functions by removing the require.
Change low-level call to a transfer to enforce revert on failure (use transfer instead of call), which can alter whether sendMoney's effects (value transfer and reverts) occur.
Perform the call and check the returned success boolean, reverting on failure, which changes whether state (balances) is affected when the external call fails silently in the original.

Ignore returned success and also capture return data (no other behavior) — explicitly assign the return to variables to change compilation-time behavior and make returned success unused, potentially affecting reentrancy/order interactions.
Invert onlyOwner require to allow only non-owners, changing who can call sendMoney and thus observable behavior after calls.
Remove the onlyOwner guard from sendMoney so anyone can invoke it, altering which callers can change balances via sendMoney.
